meta.title: OPS-SAT Firmware Modification
meta.description: This diagram captures the telecommand-driven firmware modification attack on the OPS-SAT cube sat, as described by J. Willbold et. al in  Space Odyssey: An Experimental Software Security Analysis of Satellites.

data.label: Lack of TC Authentication (from paper)
user_properties:
The COM radio is directly connected to the OBC, where the OBSW uses the CSP protocol, which offers eXtended Tiny Encryption Algorithm (XTEA) 
encryption and Hash-Based Message Authentication Codes (HMAC) authentication. However, these capabilities are disabled via a compile-time flag. 
Hence, the COM does not offer any protection, and external attackers can command the satellite by executing arbitrary TCs, which includes anyone with a custom GS.

data.label: Rogue GS
user_properties:
This corresponds to the "external attacker" model
described in the J.Willbold paper.

data.label: Ground Segment Model
user_properties: This model is inferred from the attacker model described in the paper. It is meant to capture a simplistic ground station/network.

data.label: Transmitter/Receiver Models
user_properties:
D3FEND's models of transmitters and receivers by definition incorporate front-end/back-end processing
components such as modulators/filters/etc., so they don't need to be modeled separately.

data.label: Software, Firmware, or Programmable Logic Manipulation
Space Segment Model
user_properties: Note that this is not a complete model of OPS-SAT, but rather includes the key components relevant to this attack.
